record.paper_title: Open Problems in the Function Theory of the Bergman Space
record.context_brief: Zero sequences in the Bergman space
record.original_question: Let D be the open unit disk and let L2_a(D) be the Bergman space of square-area-integrable analytic functions on D. A sequence A = {a_j} of points in D is an L2_a(D) zero sequence if there is a function in L2_a(D) whose zeros are precisely A, counted with multiplicity. Which sequences A in D are exactly the zero sequences of L2_a(D)?

evidence.quote: A sequence A = {aj}j of points in D, is said to be an L2_a(D) zero sequence if there exists a function in L2_a(D) that vanishes precisely on the sequence A, counting multiplicities.
Problem 1.2. Characterize the L2_a(D) zero sequences.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathbb{D} = \{z \in \mathbb{C} : |z| < 1\}$ denote the open unit disk, and let $L^2_a(\mathbb{D})$ denote the Bergman space of analytic functions $f : \mathbb{D} \to \mathbb{C}$ satisfying
$$\|f\|^2 = \int_{\mathbb{D}} |f(z)|^2\, dA(z) < \infty,$$
where $dA$ is Lebesgue area measure on $\mathbb{D}$. A sequence $A = \{a_j\}_{j \geq 1}$ of points in $\mathbb{D}$ (with possible repetitions to account for multiplicity) is called an $L^2_a(\mathbb{D})$ zero sequence if there exists a nonzero function $f \in L^2_a(\mathbb{D})$ whose zero set, counted with multiplicities, is precisely $A$.

Give an intrinsic characterization, in terms of the geometric or potential-theoretic distribution of the points $\{a_j\}$ in $\mathbb{D}$, of those sequences $A \subset \mathbb{D}$ that arise as zero sequences of functions in $L^2_a(\mathbb{D})$.
artifact.status_search_result: A complete characterization of zero sequences for the unweighted Bergman space $L^2_a(\mathbb{D})$ remains an open problem. Substantial partial results exist (e.g., Korenblum-type necessary conditions, Horowitz products, and Luecking's 1996 density characterization for certain weighted Bergman spaces), and recent works characterize zero sets for various weighted Bergman spaces in the spirit of Luecking, but no clean intrinsic characterization is known for $L^2_a(\mathbb{D})$.

status_evidence.title: Recent Progress and Open Problems in the Bergman Space
status_evidence.snippet: Survey listing open problems on the function theory of the Bergman space, including characterization of zero sequences.
status_evidence.claim: The characterization of zero sequences in the Bergman space is listed among open problems.

status_evidence.title: Zero sequences, factorization and sampling measures for weighted Bergman spaces
status_evidence.snippet: Zero sets characterized for Bergman spaces with certain doubling/Bekollé-Bonami weights in the spirit of Luecking's 1996 results; further open problems posed.
status_evidence.claim: Only partial characterizations exist (weighted, density-type) and several related questions remain open.
